races.race_name: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)

runners.name: Damysus
runners.spotlight: Won the Group 3 Earl Of Sefton at Newmarket (1m1f, good) on reappearance and mid-division in Group 1s on next two runs; third of five to subsequent International winner Item here (10.2f, good to firm) last time and has leading claims back down in trip/grade; cheekpieces go on; has won on good to soft.
runners.comment: Third of five to Item over 10.2f here last time; leading claims back down in trip/grade

runners.name: Saber Strike
runners.spotlight: All five starts on good/good to firm; made it 2-2 with 7f Listed win at Newmarket in May and has shaped in 7f/1m Group 3 races on his last two starts (including here) as though this new trip could be a good fit; not discounted in first-time tongue-tie; the blinkers adopted last time are left off.
runners.comment: Has shaped in 7f/1m Group 3 races on last two runs as though this trip could be a good fit

runners.name: Persica
runners.spotlight: Went very close in Group 3 Diomed Stakes at Epsom in June (8.5f, good to soft; won same race 12 months earlier) and has continued in good form, justifying even-money favouritism in Listed race at Newbury (1m2f, good to firm) last time; he's firmly in calculations.
runners.comment: Listed winner at Newbury last month and he's firmly in calculations

runners.name: Jonquil
runners.spotlight: All starts on good/faster; won the Group 2 Celebration Mile at Goodwood last August and bagged 1m Listed win at Ascot this May; close third in hot 1m1f conditions race at Goodwood three weeks ago and could be involved.
runners.comment: Group 2 winner last season; ran well at Goodwood recently and could be involved

runners.name: Ridari
runners.spotlight: Group 2 winner at Longchamp (1m, very soft) last October; not at the same level in the USA this year on his three starts for Miguel Clement but those were on firm ground and he could be a different proposition now back on a slower surface on his first start for George Scott; he's one to consider.
runners.comment: Below best on firm ground in US this year but won Group 2 on very soft last October

runners.name: King Of Earth
runners.spotlight: Promise on first three starts (including on soft/good to soft) before winning Wolverhampton maiden (8.6f, AW) in June; followed up in big-field handicap at the Curragh (1m1f, good) in first-time cheekpieces (retained); this is a much tougher test of his credentials and Tom Marquand rides stablemate Saber Strike, but he's very well bred and in top hands; not ruled out.
runners.comment: Won on handicap debut at the Curragh; this is much tougher but he's not ruled out

runners.name: Dividend
runners.spotlight: Unraced on slow ground; won two handicaps in a row at Meydan (1m1f/9.5f, good) in February before Group 2 second there (1m1f, good) and he returned from a break with good third in the Listed Wolferton Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm); things haven't gone to plan on his two starts since but a line can be put through Goodwood as he got no run; interesting contender.
runners.comment: He's shown some strong form this year and a line can be put through Goodwood (got no run)

runners.name: Hankelow
runners.spotlight: Won on debut here (7f, good) last June and made it 2-3 as 2yo when making all in the Group 3 Autumn Stakes at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) last October; reappeared with fine front-running third in the Group 1 Poule d'Essai Des Poulains at Longchamp (1m, very soft) in May; down the field in the Group 1 Prix du Jockey Club at Chantilly (10.5f, good) three weeks later but has had a break since and is very much of interest judged on his previous form.
runners.comment: Third in the French 2,000 Guineas and very much of interest judged on that form
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid

runners.name: Archivist
runners.spotlight: Unplaced favourite in the Royal Hunt Cup at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) but bounced back to win the competitive Golden Mile at Glorious Goodwood (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago; defied joint-top weight last time and he could give a good account now up in grade; has shown promise on soft.
runners.comment: Defied joint-top weight in the Golden Mile at Goodwood and could give a good account

runners.name: Geryon
runners.spotlight: 3yo who has got better with each run this season and impressed in the Group 3 Meld at Leopardstown (1m1f, good) last month before finishing second in the Group 3 Gordon at Glorious Goodwood (1m4f, good to firm) under a 3lb penalty (same today); runner-up in a Group 2 on yielding to soft last September; this versatile sort could be in the mix back down in trip.
runners.comment: 3yo who has got better with each run this season; won 1m1f Group 3 two starts ago

runners.name: Point Lynas
runners.spotlight: Slow ground would be a worry (non-runner due to unsuitable good to soft here on Thursday) and he's unraced over this far; however, this front-runner has an extremely solid record in 1m handicaps here and was a Group 2 runner-up at Ascot (1m) last July; capable of bold bid if conditions suit.
runners.comment: Slow ground would be a worry but he has a very solid record in 1m handicaps here
runners.owner: Julie And David R Martin And Dan Hall

races.race_name: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners.name: Infraad
runners.spotlight: Suited by the step up to 1m4f when getting the better of a terrific battle to win at Glorious Goodwood on second handicap start (good to firm; front two clear); 1m6f could prompt further improvement and his trainer has won two of the last seven runnings; showed promise on soft on debut; key player.
runners.comment: Dug deep for 1m4f win at Glorious Goodwood and open to further improvement now up to 1m6f

runners.name: Into The Light
runners.spotlight: Bumped into the highly progressive Lost Boys when short-headed on handicap debut at Sandown (1m2f, good; unraced on slower) in April and bounced back from an underwhelming Royal Ascot run to win at Glorious Goodwood (1m3f, good to firm) in first-time cheekpieces (retained); dam was a 15.5f Listed winner (heavy) and he could take another step forward now tackling 1m6f.
runners.comment: 1m3f win at Glorious Goodwood and pedigree suggests this longer trip will be a good fit

runners.name: Galilean Quality
runners.spotlight: Has won on various ground; strong finish for 4l sixth of 19 in the King George V Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m4f) and that handicap form has worked out exceptionally well; as expected he was suited by the step up to 1m6f when winning at Ascot last month and could have more to offer at this trip.
runners.comment: Strong finish over 1m4f at Royal Ascot and a 1m6f win there since; unexposed at the trip

runners.name: Mythical Bay
runners.spotlight: Prominent racer who showed improvement to win by 4l at Newbury (1m4f, good to soft) in June and followed up at Newmarket (1m6f, good to firm) last month; had just a nose to spare last time and is 5lb higher today but he's clearly progressive and his trainer has won three of the last six runnings.
runners.comment: He's won his last two; clearly progressive and yard has won three of the last six runnings

runners.name: Limestone
runners.spotlight: Made it four wins on the spin when landing the Group 2 Queen's Vase at Royal Ascot (1m6f, good to firm; versatile ground-wise); down the field in the Group 1 Grand Prix de Paris at Longchamp since but judged on his previous form he could be on an advantageous mark for today's handicap debut.
runners.comment: Group 2 Queen's Vase winner who could be on an advantageous mark for this handicap debut

runners.name: Tierra Del Toro
runners.spotlight: Looked one to follow when keeping on for third on handicap debut in the London Gold Cup at Newbury (1m2f, good); however, he's failed to settle and finished soundly beaten over 1m4f on his last two starts and, while Goodwood may not have suited last time, he arrives with something to prove.
runners.comment: Looked one to follow when 3rd in London Gold Cup but twice soundly beaten over 1m4f since

runners.name: Who's Lope
runners.spotlight: Won at Beverley (1m4f, good to firm) in May on third run and close second to My Ballyquinn on handicap debut over C&D in June (good; led); further improvement is necessary but he's just the type his trainer, who has won three of the last six runnings, does very well with; unraced on slow ground.
runners.comment: Second over C&D in June; needs improvement but he's just the type his trainer excels with

runners.name: My Ballyquinn
runners.spotlight: All starts on good/good to firm; made it 2-3 in handicaps when upped in trip to beat Who's Lope over C&D in June; a line can be put through his subsequent second of three at Sandown as they went no gallop; up in grade today but unexposed at the trip and he's not ruled out.
runners.comment: Won over C&D in June and a line can be put through his subsequent run; not ruled out

runners.name: Devil's Peak
runners.spotlight: He's raced ten times but has shown improved form of late, winning narrowly in a small field at Newbury (1m3f, good to firm) then second to Into The Light at Glorious Goodwood (1m3f, good to firm); stayed on well last time and could better that performance now at 1m6f; unproven on slow ground.
runners.comment: Stayed on well for 1m3f second at Glorious Goodwood; could better that form now at 1m6f

runners.name: Glory Road
runners.spotlight: Placed on first three starts (8.3f-1m2f, including on good to soft) before justifying favouritism on handicap/AW debut at Newcastle four weeks ago (12.4f; Eniac third); that latest form has been franked by the runner-up and there's every chance that this one will be suited by 1m6f; one to consider.
runners.comment: 12.4f win on handicap debut at Newcastle and that form has been franked by the runner-up

runners.name: Baltic Fleet
runners.spotlight: 2yo maiden winner (good to soft) who has run some good races in defeat in 1m4f handicaps this year, including here (good) in May and when third at Ascot (good to firm) recently in a first-time visor (retained); it's possible 1m6f will suit but others in this line-up appear to be more progressive.
runners.comment: Some good runs in defeat over 1m4f this year but others appear to be more progressive

runners.name: Sharkeyboy
runners.spotlight: Improved upon his three maiden runs (1m-9.5f) when upped to 12.3f on handicap debut at the Galway festival (yielding), beaten just a neck in that big field; he's trained by Willie Mullins and wears first-time cheekpieces today, and there can be optimism that he will continue to progress; respected.
runners.comment: Trained by Willie Mullins; went close at Galway on h'cap debut; can continue to progress

runners.name: Steel Raven
runners.spotlight: Won a maiden at Pontefract (1m2f, good) last month on his third start; it's still very early days but he finished held in sixth behind a couple of these at Glorious Goodwood (1m3f, good to firm) and others are preferred.
runners.comment: Sixth behind a couple of these at Glorious Goodwood and others are preferred

runners.name: Probation
runners.spotlight: 2-2 in handicaps, both three-runner races, the first by 12l at Lingfield (11.6f, good to firm) and the latest at Sandown (1m6f, good to firm); they went no gallop last time and, from out of the handicap, he's 8lb higher in this much hotter race, but it remains to be seen where his ceiling lies.
runners.comment: 2-2 in handicaps; they were both 3-runner races but remains to be seen where ceiling lies

runners.name: Eniac
runners.spotlight: Seven-race maiden who is 2lb out of the handicap but he showed promise for Donnacha O'Brien and ran a big race on stable debut at Newcastle (12.4f, AW) four weeks ago, travelling well and keeping on nicely for 1l third behind Glory Road; this longer trip could suit and he's an interesting contender.
runners.comment: 0-7 and 2lb out of the h'cap but ran well on stable debut and this longer trip could suit

runners.name: Bay Of Stars
runners.spotlight: Won at Dundalk (1m4f, AW) in April on second start and kept on for close second on handicap debut at Leopardstown (1m4f, good) in May behind one on the middle leg of a hat-trick; failed to settle and had to wait for a clear run when third in first-time cheekpieces (retained) at Down Royal (1m5f, soft) two months ago and that form has also been franked by the winner; a strong gallop today would help and he could be capable of considerably better.
runners.comment: Did well to finish 3rd at Down Royal last time and could be capable of considerably better

runners.name: Vantage Code
runners.spotlight: Third of 15 on the Monday of the Galway festival last month (12.3f, yielding) and found a surge of improvement in a first-time hood to demolish a big field there (1m6f, yielding to soft) four days later; hit with a whopping 15lb rise but that may not stop him given his dominance last time.
runners.comment: Demolished a big field at the Galway festival and 15lb rise may not stop him today

races.race_name: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)

runners.name: Notable Speech
runners.spotlight: Not the first time he's failed to fire at Ascot when a disappointing favourite in the Queen Anne, having previously looked better than ever in showing his trademark turn of foot to win the Lockinge at Newbury (good); renowned as a top-class domestic/international miler but he didn't run badly in last year's July Cup and should be fully effective at 7f; while fast ground shows him at his brilliant best, he nearly won a French Group 1 last season on good to soft; commands the utmost respect.
runners.comment: Top-class miler who should be fine back at 7f, but faster ground would be preferred

runners.name: Puerto Rico
runners.spotlight: Last two efforts in fast-ground Group 1s at 1m don't reflect his true ability and on going slower than good he has form figures of 114 (all on very soft) in Group 1s at 7f and 1m, with the defeat highly respectable on this season's reappearance when close up behind last weekend's Jacques le Marois winner Rayif; one to be interested in with cheekpieces given a go.
runners.comment: On ground slower than good he boasts form figures of 114 in Group 1s at 7f and 1m
runners.owner: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith

runners.name: Lake Forest
runners.spotlight: From three visits to York he's won a Gimcrack and finished an unlucky-in-running second in this 12 months ago; gelding operation has triggered a further upturn in his fortunes, winning Listed/Group 2 races over this trip (good ground) on either side of a close fifth in the 6f Group 1 sprint at Royal Ascot (running on); it was his second run in as many days at Glorious Goodwood (after winning the Lennox) when traffic issues scuppered all hope in the Sussex Stakes; the worry is this week's rain as he's had precious little racing on ground softer than good and hasn't shone when he has.
runners.comment: Returns to optimum trip after a luckless run in the Sussex; good/faster ground suits best

runners.name: Zavateri
runners.spotlight: One of the best 2yos around last season, with his head defeat of Gstaad in the Group 1 National Stakes at the Curragh (7f, yielding; unraced on softer) his most striking piece of form; a setback ruled out him out of the 2,000 Guineas after shaping encouragingly in a trial, and he got messed about at a crucial stage when fifth in the Sussex (one place behind Ten Bob Tony); this shorter trip might be a better fit for him and, as he still retains some upside, he looks a key player.
runners.comment: Top-class 2yo at 7f; plenty to like about his fifth in the Sussex (had a troubled run)

runners.name: Flora Of Bermuda
runners.spotlight: A standing dish in Group races over 6f but had long given the impression that 7f might suit and she duly saw that trip out well to take the Group 3 Oak Tree at Glorious Goodwood (good to firm; could be even better on softer); the close proximity of the third/fourth horses would suggest that a repeat performance won't get the job done here, but she's a likeable mare who should give her running, especially with form figures of 121 on her last three visits to York; respected.
runners.comment: Classy at 6f and won at Goodwood on first attempt at 7f; has an eye-catching record here

runners.name: Ten Bob Tony
runners.spotlight: Prior to this year all his best form was at 7f on ground good or slower, and yet he popped up at 50-1 in a fast-ground Queen Anne and proved that was no flash in the pan with his close fourth to Bow Echo in the Sussex Stakes (again 1m on good to firm), in which he was nearest at the finish having been held up out the back; hard to knock.
runners.comment: Won the Queen Anne and a closing fourth in the Sussex; he'll be fine back at 7f

runners.name: Paborus
runners.spotlight: Strike-rate of 5-8 and long absences are a feature in his profile; back from another to produce career-best form in beating Marvelman at Newcastle in June (6f AW) but he'd be no certainty to confirm those placings on 5lb worse terms, while there are plenty of others to worry about; on the plus side, he remains a relative unknown quantity and trip/ground will be fine.
runners.comment: Back from another absence to win a 6f Group 3 on the AW; fine at 7f but more needed here

runners.name: Marvelman
runners.spotlight: Unraced at York but he does go on any ground, and his career-best form came on soft when impressing in a 7f Group 2 at Doncaster last September; creditable effort conceding weight all round when runner-up to Paborus in a Group 3 over 6f (AW) on his return to Britain in June and it's best to put a line through his run behind Lake Forest at Glorious Goodwood (7f) as he raced far too freely off a slacking pace; with a truer gallop on the cards and no ground issues, he could be a lively one.
runners.comment: Impressed in a Group 2 on soft last season, so this week's rain brings him into it

runners.name: Satono Reve
runners.spotlight: Japanese raider who has made his name over 6f, winning two Grade 1s on home soil and placed in three British Group 1s, latterly the July Cup at Newmarket where he wasn't stopping at the finish; ran well on his only start over 7f (in 2024) and it was over 1m that he won his first ever race; an intriguing runner, though the glaring concern is that his peak efforts have come on good or faster ground and this surface is likely to be the softest he's raced on (effective on yielding back home).
runners.comment: Top-class 6f performer who wasn't stopping in last month's July Cup; ground concerns

runners.name: Lifeplan
runners.spotlight: All runs at 6f on good or faster ground; unbeaten as a 2yo, winning a weak Gimcrack here 12 months ago on his second start (good to firm); lots to like about his comeback run at Chester, as he did a lot of early running from a bad draw and was picked off only late on; however, that was a Listed race and this is a new trip, so it looks a big ask.
runners.comment: Gimcrack winner; third in a Listed race on comeback and this is a new trip for him

runners.name: Power Blue
runners.spotlight: Debut winner at two on soft and later beat this year's 1,000 Guineas heroine True Love in the Group 1 Phoenix Stakes (6f, good); no more than minor roles in three 1m Group 1s this season before justifying favouritism when his sights were lowered in a Curragh Group 2 last month (7f, good to firm); he didn't exactly blow his rivals away that day and he's probably playing for the places, for all that a fast-run race at 7f might be his ideal scenario these days.
runners.comment: Group 1 winner last season, but it was a Group 2 he won latest and that was workmanlike

runners.name: Rogue Diplomat
runners.spotlight: Seriously progressive this season in 1m handicaps, including a near miss in the Lincoln (good to soft; won on soft) and victory in the Royal Hunt Cup at Royal Ascot (good to firm); dispelled any doubts about his Group-race credentials when emerging from last in a steadily run race to push Lake Forest to a neck in the 7f Lennox at Glorious Goodwood (good); that effort deserves an upgrade, so he's in the mix.
runners.comment: Royal Hunt Cup winner; massive effort on Group-race debut when 2nd to Lake Forest

runners.name: Native Warrior
runners.spotlight: Form figures of 1311571 in a visor; a graduate from the handicap ranks and he didn't have all that much in hand when the 6-4 winner of a Group 3 in Ireland in June on latest start (7f, soft); looks up against it now he's dining at the top table, unless transformed by a wind operation.
runners.comment: Graduate from the handicap ranks; Group 3 winner last time but now dining at the top table

runners.name: Powerful Glory
runners.spotlight: Has some CV for one so lightly raced, having won the Group 2 Mill Reef (heavy) as a 2yo and added the Group 1 Champions Sprint at Ascot last October (good), beating previous Group 1 winner Lazzat; comeback run at the Curragh was a bit of a damp squib, though he was conceding weight all round in that Group 2 and he probably needed it; dangerous to dismiss, for all that he'll be into unknown territory inside today's final furlong.
runners.comment: Had only six races and has won a Group 2 and a Group 1; ventures over 7f for first time

races.race_name: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners.name: Klassleader
runners.spotlight: Just six races; came from the back when second on handicap debut at Haydock (1m6f, good to soft) last September and again when eventually well on top at York (1m4f, good; 8lb higher today) this May; the latter promised much, which was singularly unfulfilled when hot favourite at Newmarket (1m4f, good to firm) seven weeks ago; virtually first off the bridle that day but a return to 1m6f on softer ground today ensures that he remains of major interest.
runners.comment: Just six races; return to 1m6f on softer ground ensures that he remains of major interest

runners.name: Align The Stars
runners.spotlight: Not often seen on softer than good but he won on good to soft in June 2024; failed to shine at this meeting in 2024 or 2025, during a long losing run; he's broken that with two 2m wins on the AW this year, most notably in the Northumberland Plate at Newcastle in June, and also second at Newmarket (1m6f, good to firm) in May, but only mid-division behind Hopewell Rock at Goodwood three weeks ago; others seem more likely.
runners.comment: Northumberland Plate AW winner in June but others seem more likely today

runners.name: Hopewell Rock
runners.spotlight: Won on heavy as 2yo, unraced on soft; regular progress/promise (including on good to soft) in his first six handicaps, without winning; raced freely early on in the last of those when running out of steam at Royal Ascot (1m4f) but he then got his act together at Glorious Goodwood (upped to 1m6f, good to firm) three weeks ago when travelling smoothly in mid-division and going on over 1f out, before holding a hampered runner-up (who won well here on Wednesday); well treated under 4lb penalty.
runners.comment: Got his act together at Glorious Goodwood (upped to 1m6); well treated under 4lb penalty

runners.name: Spinning Wheel
runners.spotlight: Won at Leicester (1m4f, good to soft) last October and reappeared with a good second at Goodwood (1m6f, good) in May, both from the front; soft ground was likely to blame at Epsom on Derby Day but recent return to action was pretty spectacular when a change in tactics saw him come from last to first in a well-contested 13-runner race at Southwell (1m3f, AW); has a 4lb penalty after that narrow win but this lightly raced 4yo now promises better still and a good 5lb claimer is enlisted; player if the ground isn't too soft.
runners.comment: 4lb penalty after a narrow win but this lightly raced 4yo now promises better still
runners.owner: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum

runners.name: Opportunity
runners.spotlight: 2m Group 1 entry; lightly raced 4yo, unraced on softer than good except on debut; has flourished this term, winning in some style at Carlisle (1m3f) in May and Royal Ascot (1m4f; 10lb higher today) in June; backed up the latter form when second in a steadily run Group 3 at Goodwood and looks well worth a crack at 1m6f.
runners.comment: Has flourished this term, including Royal Ascot win, and looks well worth a crack at 1m6f

runners.name: Furthur
runners.spotlight: Seemed to be going places when he won a Group 3 at Newbury (1m5f, good to firm) last August, followed by a respectable sixth on soft ground in the St Leger, but he's been disappointing this term; headgear goes on.
runners.comment: Group 3 win at Newbury (1m5f) last August; disappointing this term; headgear goes on

runners.name: Love Me Tender
runners.spotlight: Half-brother to 1m1f-1m2f winner Lord Charming (including Group 3; RPR 113); unraced until last September but won over 1m1f in Germany on first two starts and beaten 2l in a 1m2f Listed race at Chantilly (very soft) in October; 180,000euros buy last November and unraced since; it looked last time as if going beyond 1m2f would suit him well and this choice of engagement is highly respected for trainer who's won two of the last three Ebors.
runners.comment: Useful when trained in Germany for three 1m1f/1m2f races last autumn; needs a close look
runners.owner: H O S Syndicate & Oti Racing

runners.name: Daiquiri Bay
runners.spotlight: 2m Group 1 entry for Ascot in October, along with several others in this; unraced on good to soft and below form in a soft-ground run last term; unbeaten in 2026, having led in the closing stages on good to firm at the Newmarket Guineas meeting (1m4f) and Royal Ascot (1m6f; by a head); raised another 5lb but progressive and plenty to like if the ground proves suitable.
runners.comment: 2-2 this season, by a head at Royal Ascot (1m6f) last time; not proven on softer than good

runners.name: Emit
runners.spotlight: Close second in 1m7f French Group 2 (on very soft) last October remains his best form; he has a competitive handicap mark, though, as he showed when running on well from off the pace to be fourth of 17 to Opportunity at Royal Ascot (1m4f) last time; Ryan Moore stays on board; Irish St Leger entry with strong claims back up in trip.
runners.comment: Running-on fourth at Royal Ascot (1m4f) last time; strong claims back up in trip

runners.name: Mr Hollywood
runners.spotlight: 2m Group 1 entry with no ground worries; 1m2f Listed and Group 3 winner in Germany and last year he scored over 1m4f in France; sole Flat run for new connections was a good one when third in the 2m5f Queen Alexandra at Royal Ascot, travelling well turning for home; followed that by knuckling down well for a maiden hurdle win at the Galway festival and his trainer has won two of the last three Ebors, but a 7lb rise since Royal Ascot isn't ideal.
runners.comment: 2m5f Queen Alexandra third at Royal Ascot before hurdles win; 7lb rise isn't ideal

runners.name: Paddy The Squire
runners.spotlight: Markedly improved last year and even better this term, all on good or good to firm, although he had lots of soft-ground form in previous seasons; wore cheekpieces when staying-on third of 16 to Daiquiri Bay at Royal Ascot (1m6f) and close second at Newmarket (1m4f) 18 days later; raised another 3lb but each-way player if the ground is okay for him.
runners.comment: Raised another 3lb but each-way player if the ground is okay for him

runners.name: Paradias
runners.spotlight: Probably acts on good to soft, much more to prove on soft; reliable 7yo who's never been better than this season (1m2f-2m); also seems to have found his limits but perhaps a handicap such as this will suit him better than the much smaller-field Group/Listed race's he's contested on last three starts.
runners.comment: Has never been better than this season (1m2f-2m); also seems to have found his limits

runners.name: Square Necker
runners.spotlight: 4yo with just five races under his belt but he has 2m Group 1 entry for Ascot in October; won handicap debut at Hamilton (1m5f, good) in May and firmly in charge from over 1f out in 12-runner race at Ayr (1m5f, soft; always prominent) in June; up another 6lb today, inexperienced and drawn almost widest of all, but he strides out as if 1m6f will suit him well and has significantly more to give.
runners.comment: 2-2 in handicaps (1m5f); inexperienced but 1m6f will suit and he has significantly more

runners.name: Ascending
runners.spotlight: Unraced on the soft on Flat for nearly two years; progressive last season, most notably on good to firm with his win at Royal Ascot (2m4f) and second in this race; failed to shine at Ascot on first two starts this season (every chance over 1f out at the Royal meeting) before never dangerous when 40-1 in a recent Leopardstown Group 3; off the same mark as 12 months ago, however, this Irish St Leger entry could be dangerous to dismiss.
runners.comment: No impact this season but he was second in this race last year off the same mark

runners.name: Beylerbeyi
runners.spotlight: Acts on good to soft but soft would be a worry; tricky to settle and is held up in rear; won the Cesarewitch at Newmarket (2m2f; 10lb higher today) last October and he's looked just as good on most starts since, without winning but late traffic woes seemingly prevented him from going close last time; without his usual jockey Billy Loughnane today but he was a close second last term under Clifford Lee; probably involved if he can get the breaks.
runners.comment: Tricky to settle and is held up in rear; probably involved if he can get the breaks

runners.name: Tarriance
runners.spotlight: Won the Melrose on this card last year before a creditable last of seven in the soft-ground St Leger (sole run on softer than good); returned to a handicap off this mark at Glorious Goodwood (again 1m6f on good to firm) three weeks ago for a good fourth of 13 to Hopewell Rock, challenging smoothly over 2f out; that was after 11 weeks off and much more encouraging again.
runners.comment: Melrose winner on this card last year; Goodwood 4th latest was much more encouraging again

runners.name: Stressfree
runners.spotlight: Probably no ground worries; not a prolific winner, with his waiting tactics, but he was fourth in the Ebor last year off a 2lb higher mark; ran creditably on reappearance, before none of his three starts since panned out favourably; can be given a place chance.
runners.comment: Not a prolific winner, with his waiting tactics, but Ebor fourth last year off 2lb higher

runners.name: Burdett Road
runners.spotlight: 2023 Royal Ascot winner who has also tasted the high life in top hurdle races; one of the market leaders in this in 2024 but came 12th; his attentions have been focused on the Flat this year but he hasn't been in peak form, 11th off this reduced mark behind Hopewell Rock last time; there's a chance that return to softer ground today will help; something needs to.
runners.comment: There's a chance that return to softer ground today will help; something needs to

runners.name: Circus Of Rome
runners.spotlight: Ran creditably twice over 1m6f last autumn, including on good to soft; this campaign is not that hard to forgive - over 1m2f/1m on first two occasions and with 2m for the Northumberland Plate (just 8-1) perhaps a stretch last time - although he has raced a bit freely; well treated judged on peak form and could be about to come good again.
runners.comment: Well treated judged on peak form (2025) and could be about to come good again

runners.name: Epic Poet
runners.spotlight: Not proven on worse than good to soft; fourth in this race in 2024; 7yo who is 0-13 since winning at Meydan in January 2025; has run really well in plenty of Group races in the interim, including the last two runnings of the Yorkshire Cup over C&D, but he ran a stinker in C&D Listed event in June and also disappointed here on latest start; big questions to answer after that.
runners.comment: Ran a stinker in C&D Listed event in June and also disappointed here on latest start

runners.name: Poetic Sound
runners.spotlight: Registered his highest rating in 1m6f Listed race on soft ground last April (his only time front-running); always prominent when strong finish took him to a handicap win at the Curragh (1m6f, yielding) this term and, although he wasn't discredited over 2m later in June, this trip on softer than good may well be the best fit; wears headgear for the first time.
runners.comment: This trip on softer than good may well be the best fit; wears headgear for the first time

runners.name: Real Dream
runners.spotlight: Rarely seen on softer than good but it used to be okay (2023); made the frame only once (Saudi Arabia in February) from seven starts this year; admittedly hampered at Newmarket six weeks ago on latest outing, a race in which he ran well last term before finishing fifth in this; 7lb lower than 12 months ago and has a place squeak but there's been no win for over three years.
runners.comment: 5th off 7lb higher in 2025 Ebor; some renewed hope last time; no win for over three years

races.race_name: Sky Bet Constantine Handicap (Heritage Handicap)

runners.name: Dance In The Storm
runners.spotlight: Has raced exclusively at 7f, winning four of her 12 starts; overcame a wide draw and trouble in running to win at Chester (7f, good) three weeks ago, showing a bright turn of foot and having more in hand than the 1l winning margin might suggest; up 4lb ahead of this belated first 6f run but the way she travels through her races offers serious encouragement that she will improve for it; tops the list.
runners.comment: Steadily progressive at 7f but this drop to sprint trips could unlock further improvement

runners.name: Far Above Dream
runners.spotlight: The winner of five of his 12 starts (5.7f-6f) since joining James Owen last summer; fourth and sixth in major handicaps on last two starts and it would seem highly likely that he will give his running once again; appears to handle any ground.
runners.comment: Big improver for James Owen; good runs in major handicaps on last two starts

runners.name: Air Force One
runners.spotlight: In good form this year and he took it to a new level when powering home to win the 5.4f handicap here on Wednesday; has had few chances at 6f (third to Stratusnine over C&D last month) and will be fine on good to soft (more to prove should it get slower); respected under a 5lb penalty.
runners.comment: Took form to new level with comfortable win here (5.4f) on Wednesday; chance under penalty

runners.name: Realign
runners.spotlight: Comfortable win at Carlisle (6f, good to firm; cheekpieces first time) in May but he has come up short in the Wokingham and Stewards' Cup since; this looks no easier and he will need to be at the top of his game.
runners.comment: Came up short in top sprint handicaps on his last two starts; this looks no less demanding

runners.name: Red Spells Danger
runners.spotlight: He has not looked back since dropping to 6f in May, winning three times including an impressive success at the Shergar Cup at Ascot (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; two solid C&D runs on his record too but a 6lb rise since Ascot, allied to slower ground, could find him out; the only 3yo in the field and that age group have won the last two renewals.
runners.comment: Fast-improving 3yo; 6lb rise for Ascot demands more and has slower ground to deal with too

runners.name: Desert Falcon
runners.spotlight: Ended 2025 with a Doncaster win and a narrow defeat in the Ayr Gold Cup (6f, soft); had a wind operation after the Ayr run but two heavy defeats this summer have seen him undergo another wind surgery; on a dangerous mark but Ayr next month might be the big target; cheekpieces back on today.
runners.comment: Close second in last year's Ayr Gold Cup; two wind ops since; cheekpieces back on today

runners.name: Evening Saigon
runners.spotlight: The winner of four of his nine starts, advancing his form to the next level when winning the Stewards' Cup at Goodwood (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago; handles soft; up 4lb but there could well be more in the tank; stable also represented by Fine Interview.
runners.comment: 4-9, hitting a new high with his Stewards' Cup win three weeks ago; contender up 4lb

runners.name: Pure Legend
runners.spotlight: Three wins in France (7f-1m) and he made a satisfactory start for Kevin Ryan when sixth of 11 in a useful race at Thirsk (1m, good) three weeks ago; has his first 6f run in this deep race.
runners.comment: Three wins over further in France; fair effort on stable debut but 6f will be new for him

runners.name: King Of Light
runners.spotlight: Won well at Windsor (6f, good to firm) in June and some stiff tasks since; still looked in form when sixth at Windsor 12 days ago but this is a tougher race and he looks vulnerable once again, even with Ryan Moore booked.
runners.comment: Has some solid form this year but this looks too demanding, even with Ryan Moore booked

runners.name: Coul Angel
runners.spotlight: Style of racing leaves him a hostage to fortune but he has the ability to win a big prize when things pan out favourably; latest C&D second has been well advertised since and he wasn't well drawn there; 2lb rise should be fine and he has form on slow ground; one to consider.
runners.comment: Needs everything to fall right but he has the ability to win a big prize granted some luck

runners.name: Pocklington
runners.spotlight: All wins on AW but he is fully effective on turf; unplaced in two C&D runs this year, however, and hopes appear to rest on the return of a visor giving him a lift.
runners.comment: Useful sprinter but unplaced in 2 C&D runs this year; return of visor not enough to tempt

runners.name: Hammer The Hammer
runners.spotlight: Big chance on his 3yo best but he hasn't got anything going in three runs in big sprint handicaps this year (had wind operation prior to his return); conditions should be fine and the new cheekpieces could give him a lift; revival not out of the question.
runners.comment: Has not found his best this year but down in the weights and now tried in cheekpieces

runners.name: Fahrenheit Seven
runners.spotlight: Began the season with two dominant 5f wins on AW; well short of his best on last three starts and there are risks attached, despite his favourable mark.
runners.comment: Big chance on AW form early in the year but he's gone off the boil more recently

runners.name: Stratusnine
runners.spotlight: Form figures of 22216 at York; Wednesday's sixth can be upgraded as he was comfortably on top of those drawn high; returning to 6f should suit and he is proven on slow ground, for all that his best efforts have been on good to firm; high on the list.
runners.comment: Goes well at York and Wednesday's sixth can be upgraded; another big run is likely

runners.name: Fine Interview
runners.spotlight: The winner of three of his five starts in cheekpieces, including a smooth success at Doncaster (6f, good to soft) on return in March; failed to fire at Epsom (6f, soft; behind Sondad) 11 weeks ago but this stablemate of Evening Saigon shouldn't be passed over lightly.
runners.comment: Talented sprinter who's ideally suited by softer than good; flopped latest; revival likely

runners.name: Toca Madera
runners.spotlight: Back in top form for David O'Meara this summer, running well twice at Glorious Goodwood and again when third of 21 here (5.4f, good) on Wednesday; tanked through Wednesday's race but didn't see it out quite so well as the front two; the worry today is that further rain has fallen and he is ideally suited by good to firm.
runners.comment: In top form and travelled powerfully here when 3rd on Wednesday; ground slower than ideal
runners.owner: L Bond & Sheikh Aymen Jawad Al Hamandi

runners.name: Annaf
runners.spotlight: Money-spinner for connections down the years; recent efforts have suggested he retains a good deal of his ability and his handicap mark is easing; beaten only 3l in a 7f Group 1 at this meeting 12 months ago; each-way shout.
runners.comment: Retains ability and likely to exploit a reduced mark soon; has course form; each-way shout

runners.name: Flash Harry
runners.spotlight: Has relatively low mileage and wasn't beaten far in the Stewards' Cup three weeks ago; this looks too competitive once again though.
runners.comment: Struggled in good races this summer; still low mileage but needs a personal best

runners.name: Golden Mind
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent but he is a smart performer, as when beating his 21 rivals at Doncaster last November (6f, heavy); raced exclusively at 7f since, with mixed results, but this mark isn't beyond him and a big run could be on the cards back down in distance.
runners.comment: Capable of smart 6f form on his day; feasibly weighted; big run could be on the cards

runners.name: Sondad
runners.spotlight: His career has been one of steady but consistent progress; won at Epsom (6f, soft) and the Currragh (6.2f, good to firm) this season and ran a sound race in the Stewards' Cup at Goodwood, perhaps finding that sharp test on fast ground inadequate; can't call upon course form but the weather has turned in his favour and he has another major handicap in him.
runners.comment: Progressive sprinter for whom the weather has turned in his favour; each-way shout

races.race_name: Julia Graves Roses Stakes (Listed Race)

runners.name: Adonius
runners.spotlight: All starts at 5f; front-runner who made it 3-3 (soft-good) with conditions race win at Chester in May and returned from a break with fine third in the Group 3 Molecomb at Glorious Goodwood; holds leading form claims and this track should suit his style.
runners.comment: Molecomb runner-up; leading form claims and this track should suit his front-running style

runners.name: Sale Shark
runners.spotlight: Won on debut at Hamilton (5f, good to firm) in May and respectable fifth in Listed races on next two starts (6f, good to firm); best run when 4l fourth in the Group 3 Molecomb at Goodwood last time (5f, good to firm; Adonius second); each-way player.
runners.comment: Fourth in the Molecomb (Adonius second) and he's an each-way player

runners.name: Hickory Lad
runners.spotlight: Second to Adonius at Chester (5f, good) in May then made all in the Woodcote conditions stakes at Epsom (6f, good to soft); he's come up short in Group 2 races on his last two starts (6f, good to firm) but shaped on each occasion as though he might benefit from this return to 5f; not discounted.
runners.comment: He's been shaping in 6f Group 2s as though he might benefit from this return to 5f

runners.name: Jaan Ki Tukri
runners.spotlight: Displayed considerable improvement in first-time cheekpieces (retained since) when easily making all in a maiden at Ffos Las (6f, good) last month on his fifth start; again showed blistering pace in the Group 2 Richmond at Goodwood (6f, good to firm) last time prior to fading; could be far more of a force today back down in trip and in grade.
runners.comment: Has shown blistering pace in these cheekpieces; could benefit from drop back in trip/grade

runners.name: El Floridita
runners.spotlight: All four starts over 5f on good to firm; massively outran his 150-1 odds when runner-up in the Group 2 Norfolk at Royal Ascot and he was a respectable fifth in the Group 3 Molecomb at Goodwood since; has around 3l to find with Molecomb runner-up Adonius but might not be far away.
runners.comment: Runner-up in the Norfolk and fifth in the Molecomb; he might not be far away

runners.name: Hanney Boy
runners.spotlight: Placed in maidens (soft/good) on first three starts before close Listed third at Naas (5f, good), and he got off the mark in a maiden at Cork (5f, good to firm) last time; however, there have been mixed messages from the Naas form and he needs to take a step forward in first-time cheekpieces.
runners.comment: Close Listed third at Naas but needs to take a step forward in first-time cheekpieces

runners.name: Dubai Champion
runners.spotlight: Comfortable win in a Hamilton maiden (5f, good to soft) in June on third start and short-headed in big-field nursery at Glorious Goodwood (6f, good to firm) subsequently under Ryan Moore, who retains the ride; he's on the up and could give another good account.
runners.comment: Short-headed in big-field nursery at Glorious Goodwood and could give another good account
runners.owner: Future Champions Racing Syn & Mps Racing

runners.name: Dance A Jig
runners.spotlight: Runner-up on first two starts (5f, good to soft/good to firm), behind a notable rival on the second occasion, and bounced back from a heavy 6f Listed defeat at Royal Ascot with cosy win in small-field nursery at Haydock (5f, good); this attractively bred colt is respected back up in grade.
runners.comment: Cosy nursery win at Haydock recently and he's respected back up in grade

runners.name: Silesia
runners.spotlight: She's finished in the first three on all four starts (5f/6f, good to soft-good to firm); capable of winning races but a transformation is needed if she's to come out on top in this one.
runners.comment: In the first three on all four starts but transformation needed to win this

runners.name: Dorigo
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in two 6f maidens (AW/good), the latest a big field at Glorious Goodwood, either side of a respectable seventh of 25 in the Listed Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm); he's hung on his last two starts but stall 1 should help in that regard and this pacy sort could be suited by today's first crack at 5f; each-way possibilities.
runners.comment: He's hung left so stall 1 could help; could be suited by today's first crack at 5f

runners.name: Roots In Touche
runners.spotlight: Second on debut in the Hilary Needler at Beverley (5f, good to firm) and bounced back from a disappointing run at Catterick (5f, good to firm) with easy win in a match at Nottingham (5f, good to firm; beat a newcomer); others have a lot more substance to their form but it's hard to identify the limit of her ability; this £165,000 breeze-up buy is not ruled out each-way.
runners.comment: Others have a lot more substance to their form but she's unexposed; not ruled out each-way

races.race_name: Sky Bet Dav Reid Finale Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners.name: Raammee
runners.spotlight: Has raced only on good/good to firm when on turf; 4yo who was having only the fifth start of his career when landing the 22-runner John Smith's Cup over C&D six weeks ago; an 8lb rise means a Group-class performance will be needed to follow up but no surprise were he to find it.
runners.comment: Just fifth start when winning John Smith's Cup over C&D; up 8lb but likely more to come

runners.name: Salam Dubawi
runners.spotlight: Won at Hamilton (1m1f, good) in May on second start for yard and third past the post (demoted to fifth) to Raammee in John Smith's Cup over C&D (good to firm) in July; weakened quickly at Ascot four weeks ago but he has already shown this season that he's capable of bouncing back from a poor run.
runners.comment: Third past post in John Smith's Cup over C&D; could bounce back from poor run latest

runners.name: Castle Stuart
runners.spotlight: Won on soft as 2yo; good C&D record includes a third in this race last year and two placed efforts (latterly John Smith's Cup) in a hood this summer; the hood was left off when well beaten over 1m4f at Ascot a fortnight ago but returns now; capable of bouncing back with each-way claims at a venue which suits, particularly with the yard going well.
runners.comment: A good C&D record includes a third in this last year; each-way claims with yard going well

runners.name: Al Aali
runners.spotlight: Back to form with a bang in blinkers last month and built on his win in a small field at Newmarket by following up in a 17-runner Glorious Goodwood handicap (1m2f, good; acts on good to soft) with four of today's rivals behind; should remain competitive off 5lb higher.
runners.comment: Back to form with a bang since blinkered, including Glorious Goodwood win

runners.name: Dark Moon Rising
runners.spotlight: Back to form with a bang when scoring comfortably over C&D (good to firm) six weeks ago, his 20th outing at this track; retains handicapping scope on old form after a 6lb rise but he's yet to win back to back.
runners.comment: Comfortable winner over C&D latest but yet to win back to back in his 46-race career

runners.name: Quai De Bethune
runners.spotlight: Progressive 3yo for Andrew Balding in the first half of last year, culminating in a 1m2f handicap win at Royal Ascot (good to firm); sold for 775,000gns the following month but comfortably held in three major 1m2f handicaps on return for new yard this summer; back to only 1lb above the mark he defied at Royal Ascot but a leap of faith is needed.
runners.comment: Royal Ascot winner last season but has struggled in three outings for current yard

runners.name: Parole d'Oro
runners.spotlight: Unraced on softer than good; latest seventh of 17 to Al Aali at Glorious Goodwood was respectable but took his handicap record to 0-9; others are preferred for win purposes again.
runners.comment: Latest 7th of 17 to Al Aali at Goodwood was respectable but took handicap record to 0-9

runners.name: Diego El Queso
runners.spotlight: Progressive this year, finishing strongly to win at Leopardstown (1m2f, yielding to soft) in April; good second back there three months later and an eye-catcher when sixth of 17 to Al Aali at Glorious Goodwood (1m2f, good) since, finishing strongly having been denied a clear run and still had plenty to do over 1f out; bold show on the cards.
runners.comment: Eye-catcher at Glorious Goodwood and major player from the same mark

runners.name: Erzindjan
runners.spotlight: Fourth in the John Smith's Cup over C&D and Cambridgeshire over 1m1f at Newmarket (both good to firm) on joining this yard last year and opened the current campaign with a win back at Newmarket (1m1f, good to firm again) in May; another creditable effort when sixth of 28 in Royal Hunt Cup at Ascot since, despite leaving the impression even a stiff 1m was a little on the short side; had winning form on softer than good in Ireland much earlier in his career; likely to be on the premises.
runners.comment: Several good efforts in strong handicaps for this yard (including C&D); likely to go well

runners.name: Shafdar
runners.spotlight: Winner at Epsom (8.5f, good) in April; best run since when close fourth of 15 at Glorious Goodwood (1m1f, good to firm) in a first-time tongue-tie (retained) three weeks ago; can race freely but the Goodwood effort suggests 1m2f could be within range; enters calculations.
runners.comment: Good fourth of 15 over 1m1f at Glorious Goodwood, suggesting 1m2f could be within range

runners.name: Nepal
runners.spotlight: Acts on good to soft; won in Britain and Bahrain during his spell with George Scott; off five months (had wind surgery) and shaped as if needing the race when last of four at Redcar (1m2f) for new yard five weeks ago; his claims aren't obvious.
runners.comment: Last of four on yard debut five weeks ago, so his claims aren't obvious

runners.name: Rainbow Nebula
runners.spotlight: Progressive last autumn and rediscovered that thread to win at Redcar (1m, good) in May; hasn't been running badly over about 1m2f subsequently but needs something extra if he's to take this.
runners.comment: Handicapper in charge since Redcar win in May and this 4yo needs to find something extra

runners.name: Have Secret
runners.spotlight: Won at Pontefract (1m2f, good) in April; respectable fifth of 15 over C&D (good) at the Dante meeting in May but well held twice since, latterly at 100-1 in the John Smith's Cup.
runners.comment: In good form in the spring but needs to bounce back from lesser efforts on last two starts

runners.name: Mr Swivell
runners.spotlight: Scored twice in 2024 and three times in 2025; back to best when second in useful 1m handicap here (good to firm; acts on soft) last month but only eighth of 11 at Thirsk since and his peak RPRs (including all wins) have been achieved at about 1m.
runners.comment: Second over 1m here last month but not so good at Thirsk since; others are more obvious

runners.name: Dain Ma Nut In
runners.spotlight: Formerly a miler but has gained last three wins over 1m2f, including this race on good (made all) last year; latest success came in Bahrain in January; well beaten in the John Smith's Cup on his return to Britain but bounced straight back with a career-best second of 11 over 1m at Thirsk (good) under Lexie Clarkson three weeks ago; going softer than good would be a slight question mark.
runners.comment: Won this race last year and latest Thirsk second was a career-best RPR

runners.name: Bourbon Blues
runners.spotlight: Group placed as 2yo and he's run well in top 3yo only handicaps over 1m2f this summer, finishing second of 14 at Glorious Goodwood (good to firm; probably acts on good to soft) off this mark last time; respected with Oisin Murphy taking the reins for the first time.
runners.comment: Another good effort in a top 3yo handicap when second at Glorious Goodwood; respected
runners.owner: M Hughes, M Kerr-Dineen And Partners

runners.name: Double Parked
runners.spotlight: C&D winner on good in June but held off this mark in a Class 3 over 1m1f at Hamilton 11 days ago and this is even harder.
runners.comment: C&D win in June but fifth off this mark at Hamilton since; others are more likely

runners.name: Sujet
runners.spotlight: Two wins (1m1f/1m, good) for Dermot Weld in Ireland last year; second start for current yard when runner-up at Chester (7f, good) in May; three poor runs followed but back to form in blinkers (retained here) when second of nine back at Chester (extended 7f, good) six weeks ago; needs to prove his stamina and that he can string good efforts together.
runners.comment: Best runs for current over about 7f at Chester, so this is a different test

runners.name: Thunder Run
runners.spotlight: His two wins here came on good to firm but he also acts on soft; respectable seventh of 22 to Raammee in the John Smith's Cup over C&D (good to firm) latest; being eased 2lb is a help but it may not be quite enough.
runners.comment: Two wins here; respectable seventh of 22 to Raammee in the C&D John Smith's Cup latest

runners.name: Accredit
runners.spotlight: Bred to stay 1m2f; all three 2yo starts were on softer than good, with a promising debut before he easily justified long odds-on favouritism over 1m in a maiden at Sandown and novice at Haydock (by 11l); this is a slightly belated reappearance and he has a tricky draw for one so inexperienced, but his untapped potential is obvious.
runners.comment: Two easy 1m wins on soft/good to soft as a juvenile; has obvious untapped potential

runners.name: Dhahabi
runners.spotlight: Ended his time with Charlie Appleby on a low note (March 2024) and no revival in his four races at Meydan for another yard the following winter; 483 days off and switched stables again before well beaten at Epsom and Goodwood this summer; lots to prove.
runners.comment: No show at Epsom or Goodwood for new yard this summer; lots to prove

races.race_name: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap

runners.name: Asuka
runners.spotlight: Absent nearly two years after making a winning debut at Newmarket in 2024, he has made up for lost time recently and bagged his third win on handicap debut at Thirsk (7f, good; 15-8) three weeks ago; there should be plenty more to come from him and he needs to be taken seriously here off 3lb higher.
runners.comment: Bagged his third win on handicap debut at Thirsk (7f, good; 15-8) three weeks ago.
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid

runners.name: Rhoscolyn
runners.spotlight: Hasn't fired yet this term but needs conditions softer than good to show his best form; has dropped down to a tempting mark but is 0-3 around here and is at his best at Goodwood and Epsom.
runners.comment: Hasn't fired yet this term but needs conditions softer than good to show his best form.

runners.name: Blue Prince
runners.spotlight: Normally ridden to be produced late, as when successful at Salisbury (7f, good) in June, but was given a straightforward ride to land a claimer over C&D (good) 20 days ago; this looks tougher however and more is required.
runners.comment: Normally produced late but given a straightforward ride to land a C&D claimer 20 days ago.

runners.name: Aqpan
runners.spotlight: Made a winning return in a Southwell maiden (7f, AW) in March but found out in three Group/Listed races subsequently; gelded before his ninth of 13 at Goodwood (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago on handicap debut; looks a shade high in the weights.
runners.comment: Gelded before ninth of 13 at Goodwood (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago on handicap debut

runners.name: U Sure Do
runners.spotlight: Landed his third race when successful from a flag start at Ripon (6f, good) in May; may have needed the run when sixth of 12 at Hamilton (6f, good) on his first run since 11 days ago; races beyond 7f for the first time.
runners.comment: Landed his third race when successful from a flag start at Ripon in May.

runners.name: Collecting Coin
runners.spotlight: Formerly trained by Jessica Harrington in Ireland where he won a Galway maiden; sold to join current yard for 33,000gns last month and made an immediate impact by winning over C&D (good); has been raised 7lb and has an outside draw but may still have more to offer.
runners.comment: Made an immediate impact for new yard when winning over C&D last month.

runners.name: Yanifer
runners.spotlight: Yet to fire this season but landed his third win here when successful in this race last year (good to firm) off 4lb higher; he has also been placed twice at this track and can never be written off around here.
runners.comment: Landed his third course win when successful in this race last year off 4lb higher.

runners.name: Goldmoyne
runners.spotlight: Hasn't won on turf for over two years but landed a four-timer on the AW in the spring; has been running consistently on turf since, admittedly starting to look exposed but he should run his race.
runners.comment: Hasn't won on turf for over two years but landed a four-timer on the AW in the spring.

runners.name: Vixey
runners.spotlight: 7lb higher than her last winning mark but has a course record of 1212; cannot be written off.
runners.comment: 7lb higher than her last winning mark but course record of 1212; cannot be written off.

runners.name: Five Ways
runners.spotlight: Landed a Group 3 at Kempton last September as a juvenile before finishing fourth in the Middle Park Stakes at Newmarket, both over 6f; highly tried without success this term and although his yard is going great guns, his mark looks high at present.
runners.comment: Highly tried without success so far this term and his mark looks high at present.

runners.name: Henlein
runners.spotlight: Previously trained in Australia, he still looks to be finding his level in Britain after three unplaced efforts; dons first-time cheekpieces but best watched until he tells us more.
runners.comment: Ex-Australian, he still looks to be finding his level in Britain; first-time cheekpieces
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid

runners.name: Whip Cracker
runners.spotlight: 0-16 on turf but usually runs his race; runner-up at this track (10.5f, good) when last seen in May; may find this on the sharp side having not been seen in races less than 1m since his juvenile days.
runners.comment: Runner-up at this track when last seen in May.

runners.name: Two Tempting
runners.spotlight: First of two wins over C&D came in this contest in 2024 off 4lb lower; had a fruitful AW winter campaign; reported to have met with a setback when being readied for Chester's May meeting and returned only when beating just one home in the Golden Mile at Goodwood (1m, good to firm) recently; has a high draw to contend with here and is 3lb higher than his last winning mark.
runners.comment: First of two wins over C&D came in this contest in 2024; behind at Goodwood latest start.

races.race_name: Virgin Bet Chester Stakes (Listed Race)

runners.name: By The Book
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 5yo who progressed into a really smart performer at up to 1m6f at Meydan over the winter and made a sound return to Britain when chasing home Al Aasy in a Beverley Listed race (1m4f, good to firm) seven weeks ago; going on the soft side of good would be an unknown but he holds good form claims.
runners.comment: Did well at Meydan over winter; good return to Britain when second last month; key player

runners.name: Lazy Griff
runners.spotlight: Chased home Lambourn in last year's Chester Vase and Derby (also third to him in the Irish Derby); missed the second half of last season but showed he's still as good as ever when defeating the reopposing Lady Vivian in 2m Sandown Listed race (good) last month; raced freely and weakened quickly in the Goodwood Cup with cheekpieces added (quickly discarded) but he can bounce back with his sights lowered today.
runners.comment: Beat Lady Vivian to win 2m Listed race in July; likely best to ignore Goodwood Cup run

runners.name: Fantasy World
runners.spotlight: Sold for 600,000gns after winning a 1m6f Ascot Listed race (good to soft) for Andrew Balding last autumn; didn't make the expected impact over hurdles for Nicky Henderson earlier this year (pulled up in Triumph at Cheltenham when last seen) but resumes his Flat career back with a yard which is in tremendous form.
runners.comment: Listed win on good to soft at 3; struggled over hurdles but may fare better back on Flat

runners.name: Orchard Keeper
runners.spotlight: Reliable type whose wins have come in 1m2f and 1m6f handicaps; good fourth in this race 12 months ago and showed she retains her ability when fifth in another Listed event at Newmarket (1m4f, good to firm) on her reappearance three weeks ago.
runners.comment: Useful mare who was fourth in this last year; showed she retains ability on recent return

runners.name: Lady Vivian
runners.spotlight: Her previous course visit resulted in a handicap win over the extended 1m4f on good ground (acts on good to soft) at the 2025 May meeting; campaigned at Group/Listed level since, running her best race when 2.75l second of four to Lazy Griff at Sandown (2m, good) last month; 3lb better off with Charlie Johnston's charge this time; Ralph Beckett has won this three times since 2021.
runners.comment: Course winner; good second to Lazy Griff latest and Ralph Beckett does well in this race

runners.name: Tactician
runners.spotlight: Progressed into a useful staying handicapper in the second half of 2024; gelded ahead of this belated return; has plenty to find on form and might be using this as a prep ahead of a return to handicap company (entered in Cesarewitch).
runners.comment: With top yard but off since autumn 2024 and has plenty to find on form

runners.name: Midak
runners.spotlight: Won Group 3 at Saint-Cloud (10.5f, good) last May; respectable efforts at Listed/Group 3 level for current yard this summer but will need to pull out more for the longer trip if he's to resume winning ways.
runners.comment: Respectable efforts in similar races of but more needed to resume winning ways

runners.name: Duraji
runners.spotlight: Fine third from the front in the Chester Cup (2m2f, good) on his first start for Richard Hughes; proved way too headstrong to give himself a chance of lasting home in the Copper Horse at Royal Ascot next time but ridden with restraint and saw things out a lot better when fourth of seven in 2m Newbury handicap (good to firm) since; has a bit to find on the figures back at Listed level.
runners.comment: Third in Chester Cup in May; also creditable fourth latest but bit to find at this level

races.race_name: Powells Jewellery EBF Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.name: Nicely
runners.spotlight: Second on debut and put that experience to good use when comfortably seeing off four rivals at Hamilton (6f, good to firm) last month; didn't get home over 7f in a French Group 3 three weeks ago; has the inside stall and she holds solid claims back down in trip and class.
runners.comment: Impressive on second start (6f, good to firm); stretched by 7f latest (Group 3); contender

runners.name: The Can Can Queen
runners.spotlight: Her Listed third at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) is head and shoulders above her other four runs; drawn widest and may prove vulnerable to less-exposed rivals.
runners.comment: Listed 3rd at Newmarket reads well but it is head and shoulders above her other efforts

runners.name: Kentucky Rain
runners.spotlight: Promising second behind a smart 2yo at Goodwood on debut; struggled at Royal Ascot before a bloodless success at Beverley (5f, good to firm); not at her best in a French Listed race two weeks ago; steps up to 6f for the first time; has the form to feature.
runners.comment: Has some solid 5f form; back down in class and holds form claims now upped to 6f

runners.name: Gladys Pugh
runners.spotlight: Two runs at York, showing better form on the second occasion when missing out by a short-head four weeks ago (6f, good to firm; solid form); remains capable of better and she looks set for a big run.
runners.comment: Latest York second looks strong form and she's open to further progress; high on the list
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid

runners.name: Bated Benevolence
runners.spotlight: Down the field in the Albany Stakes at Royal Ascot but that is sandwiched by 6f wins at Nottingham (good) and Wolverhampton (AW); slower ground to contend with today but this Cheveley Park entrant is well drawn and shouldn't be far away if handling it.
runners.comment: Well held at Royal Ascot but 6f wins either side of it; decent shout if handling ground

runners.name: Jazz Queen
runners.spotlight: Her best run came at Chester (5.5f, good) but she looks exposed now and others bring much more compelling claims.
runners.comment: Best run came at Chester but her limitations seem well established now

runners.name: Takaaful
runners.spotlight: Ran green when coming off the bridle on her debut at Newbury (6f, good to firm) five weeks ago; open to improvement but she has a useful standard to aim at in this field.
runners.comment: Green but shaped nicely on last month's Newbury debut; open to progress but needs it

races.race_name: British Stallion Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.name: Lady Of Hay
runners.spotlight: Modest RPRs in two 6f fillies' maidens this summer; should be quick enough for the drop in trip but she will need to improve for it.
runners.comment: Modest RPRs in two 6f runs this summer; drops in trip with improvement essential

runners.name: Duty's Call
runners.spotlight: Finished last of eight at Sandown (5f, good to firm) on her debut four weeks ago but she was sent off favourite; bred to do much better and that initial experience won't have been lost on her.
runners.comment: Didn't live up to market billing on debut but she is bred to leave that well behind

runners.name: Angel Ceecee
runners.spotlight: First foal; dam unraced sister to winners Al Hamdany (useful 1m-1m4f including 2yo/KSA) and Schwartz (1m5f-2m), half-sister to winners Indigo Times (1m5f-2m) and Fox Kasper (8.7f-11.5f); drawn widest on debut and perhaps best watched.
runners.comment: Not really bred for 5f; represents a top yard but others are more appealing

runners.name: Ivory Moon
runners.spotlight: 700,000gns yearling; second foal of a French Group-placed 5f 2yo winner (RPR 98), herself a half-sister to French winners Allure (1m7f) and Aniyla (1m1f); holds a Cheveley Park entry; makes her debut in a winnable race and she is of obvious interest.
runners.comment: 700,000gns yearling; dam a useful 5f winner; Cheveley Park entrant; interesting newcomer

runners.name: Lady Titania
runners.spotlight: Down the field in two 6f runs this summer (tongue tied latest, absent today); drops to 5f with a point to prove.
runners.comment: Down the field in two 6f runs this summer; drops to 5f with a point to prove

runners.name: Dadawada
runners.spotlight: Made a low-key debut for Gemma Tutty at Musselburgh (5f, good) in June; withdrawn having played up at the start at Ayr this month (300-1 at the time of withdrawal); no appeal.
runners.comment: 300-1 prior to being withdrawn at Ayr on intended stable debut; no appeal

races.race_name: Kore Systems Handicap

runners.name: Alfa Duplicate
runners.spotlight: Prominent racer; three wins earlier in the season and she ran as well as she ever has when second of eight at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) last month; well drawn to attack; handles good to soft but unraced on slower.
runners.comment: Three wins this year and better than ever when second at Doncaster last month; well drawn

runners.name: U S S Charleston
runners.spotlight: Easy 5f win on soft ground at Yarmouth in May; fine second of 18 at Glorious Goodwood last month before looking stretched by 6f at Brighton 15 days ago; high on the list back at 5f.
runners.comment: 5f on slow ground no problem; strong claims if reproducing his Goodwood effort

runners.name: Dragon Spin
runners.spotlight: Good series of efforts ground to a halt at York (5.4f, good to firm) 29 days ago; needs a full revival but she has run well on soft so rain wouldn't be an issue.
runners.comment: Good run of form ground to a halt at York last month; needs a full revival

runners.name: Big Fun
runners.spotlight: Promise as a 2yo and his seasonal return at Thirsk was encouraging too; not at his best at Musselburgh 15 days ago but he is edging down the weights.
runners.comment: Not at his best last time but this isn't a strong race and he can't be discounted

runners.name: Kanishka
runners.spotlight: 7f winner who stays 1m; no threat in two sprint runs for Ian Williams; will be of more interest when stepped back up in trip.
runners.comment: No impact in two sprint runs since joining Ian Williams; of more interest when back at 7f+

runners.name: Hanney Girl
runners.spotlight: Attracted support at Beverley (5f, good to firm) ten days ago and didn't run badly in fourth of the ten runners; seems to handle any ground and she is one to consider.
runners.comment: Fair fourth from the front at Beverley ten days ago; on a handy mark; respected

runners.name: Henrythenate
runners.spotlight: Never dangerous but did keep on steadily for fourth over C&D (good ground) four weeks ago; something to prove on slower than good.
runners.comment: Fair fourth over C&D last month; something to prove on slower than good

races.race_name: Powells Jewellery Handicap

runners.name: Station X
runners.spotlight: Two wins this year, the latest a front-running C&D success in June; solid third off this mark at Hamilton 11 days ago; has other pace to contend with this time.
runners.comment: Two front-running wins this year, including C&D; has other pace to deal with this time

runners.name: Westport
runners.spotlight: Won three novice events in the spring; well held in his two handicaps but this is a drop in class and he may yet tap back into that early promise.
runners.comment: Won three novices in the spring but well beaten in both handicaps; needs a full revival
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid

runners.name: American Style
runners.spotlight: He has been revived by a switch to AW of late, finishing a close third at Wolverhampton (6f) last month before a dominant win back at that track 22 days ago; up 6lb but still feasibly weighted on his turf best; big player from a handy draw.
runners.comment: Back in form on AW in July; up 6lb for latest win but still of interest on 3yo turf best

runners.name: Brighton Boy
runners.spotlight: 7f win at Thirsk in May and also went close over 7f here a fortnight later; not so good since, including when dropped to 6f at Ripon last week.
runners.comment: Two good 7f runs, including here, in May; less good since and more to prove at 6f

runners.name: Supreme King
runners.spotlight: Series of good runs this year, most recently a dominant success at Salisbury (6f, good to firm) ten days ago; that wasn't far off his very best and he's one to consider up 4lb.
runners.comment: Arrives in top form, winning comfortably at Salisbury ten days ago; good chance

runners.name: Postmodern
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 3yo; didn't run badly in a C&D handicap (good; hooded first time) last month; slower ground and stall 13 are obvious concerns this time; change of headgear.
runners.comment: Unexposed and ran okay here last month; draw/ground concerns this time; new headgear

runners.name: Stanley Spencer
runners.spotlight: Won four times on AW for James Tate; good second at Southwell (6f) when last seen in April; sold for 13,000gns later that month; switching to turf is the obvious concern as he has been unplaceed in three previous runs on grass.
runners.comment: Four-time AW winner but rarely tackled turf for former yard; best watched

runners.name: Fortification
runners.spotlight: Big chance on this year's best efforts but his form dipped at York in June and last week's Great St Wilfrid seventh wasn't great either; unraced on slower than good; not sure what to expect.
runners.comment: Big chance on this year's best but below that level on his last two starts

runners.name: Coachello
runners.spotlight: Not the force of old but handicapped accordingly; only seen once since February and he didn't offer a great deal; usually held up so he will need plenty of luck in running from the inside stall.
runners.comment: Not the force of old but handicapped accordingly; absent since modest run in May

runners.name: Roman Dragon
runners.spotlight: Back to the mark off which he won a 5f handicap at the May meeting; not had optimal conditions since but returning to 6f and dropping in class could see a revival from this eight-time course winner.
runners.comment: Prolific course winner; drops in trip and class and can go well off a winning mark

runners.name: Reciprocated
runners.spotlight: Won his first two starts (6f, good and soft); generally struggled since but his reappearance third at Pontefract (only run in cheekpieces) was a promising effort; sold for 58,000gns since latest; starts out for David Loughnane off a reduced mark; worth a market check.
runners.comment: Conditions should suit; didn't progress for Karl Burke; sold 58,000gns since latest

races.race_name: Celebrate National Racehorse Week Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners.name: Sea And Sun
runners.spotlight: Second in his first two races but easily best form when fourth of eight in novice at Doncaster on third outing; handicap debut was at Glorious Goodwood (again 1m4f on good to firm) and he ran creditably from the front to be fifth of eight; improvement is needed but this longer trip could be interesting.
runners.comment: Improvement is needed in his second handicap but this longer trip could be interesting

runners.name: Dino Bellagio
runners.spotlight: Made all twice last season, latterly in good style over 1m6f here (heavy) in September; just 1lb higher today after lesser shows this term but the latest was a step back in the right direction and he stays 2m; case can be made.
runners.comment: Made all in good style over 1m6f here (heavy) last September; just 1lb higher today

runners.name: St Mawes
runners.spotlight: Bit to prove on softer than good; two wins followed by two Goodwood places on his only four appearances over 2m for Emma Lavelle; first run for new connections was voided before the race warmed up; made most when well beaten trying 2m4f in a Class 2 at Glorious Goodwood three weeks ago but has a competitive mark in this Class 4.
runners.comment: Well beaten trying 2m4f in a Class 2 at Glorious Goodwood; competitive mark in Class 4

runners.name: Cranachan
runners.spotlight: Won a five-runner maiden at Catterick (1m4f, good; unraced on softer) in April; sent handicapping for both starts since and his rallying second of four in the added blinkers at Newmarket (1m4f, good to firm; raced lazily) last time was an advance; it also looked encouraging for going beyond 1m4f.
runners.comment: Latest start was an advance in blinkers; it also looked encouraging for going beyond 1m4f

runners.name: Kuredu King
runners.spotlight: Won 11.6f and 1m6f (good to soft) handicaps last year for the Gosden yard; Flat reappearance fourth over C&D in May was respectable but two lesser displays (1m6f/1m4f) have followed; others have more pressing claims.
runners.comment: Flat reappearance fourth (C&D) was respectable; two lesser displays (1m6f/1m4f) followed

runners.name: Midnight Rumble
runners.spotlight: 1-22 for Alan King, with his sole win in June 2024; had a respectable first two runs for new yard over C&D this season, before tailed off on good to firm at York four weeks ago; now 6lb below his peak mark.
runners.comment: Respectable first two runs for yard over C&D, before tailed off on good to firm at York

runners.name: Howth
runners.spotlight: Last seen on Flat in 2024 for Mick Appleby and has a chance if resuming in similar vein; 4-8 as a fairly useful hurdler (ran respectably on latest start) for current yard since; considered.
runners.comment: 4-8 as a fairly useful hurdler (ran respectably on latest start); considered

runners.name: Venezuelan
runners.spotlight: Edging down weights for new yard; first three of those four runs were here and the second piece of form (2m, good; unraced on softer) gives him a chance.
runners.comment: First three of last four runs were here and the second piece of form gives him a chance

runners.name: Westerton
runners.spotlight: Ex-Alan King, with new yard this year; overall 0-7 over hurdles and 1-22 on the Flat; return to this sphere over 1m4f here (20-1) three weeks ago wasn't greatly persuasive but he is well down the weights.
runners.comment: 0-7 over hurdles and 1-22 on the Flat; well down the weights

races.race_name: Coolmore Stud St Mark's Basilica Irish EBF Maiden

runners.name: Kokoshanelle
runners.spotlight: Coulsty filly; fourth foal; dam 6f 2yo winner, half-sister to winners Ultra Cool (7f-1m2f) and Ultra Pride (1m/1m2f), out of 1m winner.
runners.comment: Coulsty filly; fourth foal; dam 6f 2yo winner, half-sister to two winners

runners.name: Heralds March
runners.spotlight: Homebred Mehmas gelding; third foal; dam 1m2f winner, half-sister to 6f-1m winner Hammer Gun, out of 1m2f winning half-sister to Australian 1m2f Group 1 winner Kingdom Of Fife.
runners.comment: Homebred Mehmas gelding; third foal; dam 1m2f winner, half-sister to 6f-1m winner

runners.name: Iveagh House
runners.spotlight: Starspangledbanner brother to 7f 2yo winner The Marty Party; dam 2m AW winner, closely related to Group-placed 10.6f winner The Anvil, half-sister to winners Glowing (7f Group 3) and Glaring (useful French 1m4f); holds several Group 1 entries.
runners.comment: Starspangledbanner brother to 7f 2yo winner The Marty Party; holds several Group 1 entries

runners.name: Knockcurra Dream
runners.spotlight: Calyx half-brother to five winners including Gazelle D'Or (Listed-placed 5f/6f inc 2yo; RPR 100), Amanirenas (6f-1m), Cheerful Chap (2m-2m5f hurdle) and So Lonely (2m hurdle); dam maiden.
runners.comment: Calyx half-brother to five winners including Gazelle D'Or (Listed-placed 5f/6f inc 2yo)

runners.name: Salt Lake
runners.spotlight: Persian Force colt; 135,000gns Y; closely related to 5f winner West Acre (inc 2yo/AW/UAE Group 2), half-brother to winners Lady Iman (5f/6f 2yo inc Group 3) and Succession (5f 2yo); dam Group-placed 6f 2yo winner.
